items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: I said, you remember Jimmie Lunceford -- would tell you what you do (inaudible) it's simple.

ctx.x: He asked me this. I said, Earl, I'm so glad you asked me. Now I can tell you because I didn't know what to say before. I says, you know one thing. You're not relating to people because they don't know about how many notes you play, and they can't follow it. And this when I went back
to tell (inaudible) I said, you remember Jimmie Lunceford -- would tell you what you do (inaudible) it's simple. The average public can relate to it. They can't relate to what you play.
I say, if you stay more melodic -- he say, well, I know melodies. He went to King Records, man, and everything he was playing was melodies.

items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: the only band I went backstage on was Jimmy Lunceford's because of Joe Thomas.

ctx.x: But I need them like I need another hole in the head, Ellen, because I have to make my own way. They made me do this. I had guys that come down to Houston that I admired, respected, and I'm in the buzzard group. You know what the buzzard group is? In the Majestic Theater where Blacks had to go to catch the Cab Callaways, the Lucky Millinders, the Jimmie Luncefords, you listen to me, unless I
went backstage, and the only band I went backstage on was Jimmy Lunceford's because of Joe Thomas.
What do you mean, the buzzards?
